warrior/protection@tank#0.desc: The go-to tank build: balances survival and threat. Skips most rage-saving talents (little use in raids) and takes Enrage, Deflection and Anticipation.

warrior/protection@tank#1.desc: Balanced like the Standard build, but takes Impale and Deep Wounds, so it scales better; Rend becomes part of the rotation. Includes Vanguard, handy outside boss fights.

warrior/protection@tank#2.desc: Trades a little survival for more damage and threat; best when you are slightly over-geared. Still uses Shield Block and Revenge, plus Bloodthirst and Death Wish. Blood Craze and Gore Drinker help in dungeons and solo play.

warrior/protection@tank#3.desc: No Protection talents. Only for fights against enemies whose attacks cannot be blocked (some elementals); otherwise you take much more damage for little gain.

warrior/protection@tank#4.desc: Relaxed dungeon tanking: stay in Defensive Stance with high Enrage uptime against groups.

warrior/protection@tank#5.desc: The highest-damage tank build: Sweeping Strikes spreads Revenge and Cleave. Needs stance dancing.
warrior/protection@tank#5.weapons: A slow weapon (the guide names Thrash Blade)

warrior/protection@tank#6.desc: PvP control: a long stun (Concussion Blow), a silence (Improved Shield Bash) and Disarm; holds up well in melee 1v1.

warrior/arms@dps#0.desc: The standard Arms PvE build, deep in Arms for Mortal Strike. Enrage is the flexible pick.

warrior/arms@dps#1.desc: Rage is scarce in PvP, so the Improved Heroic Strike points move into Deflection for survival. Flexible: Improved Slam, Spearing Strike, Enrage.

warrior/arms@dps#2.desc: For questing: skips Improved Bloodrage and Improved Heroic Strike to save rage and health.

warrior/fury@dps#0.desc: Takes every core Fury talent (Death Wish, Bloodthirst, Flurry), plus Arms talents for freer Overpower use and Impale.

warrior/fury@dps#1.desc: Dungeon version: drops Improved Berserker Rage for Lingering Rage and a full Enrage, strong when you take constant damage.

warrior/fury@dps#2.desc: Fury is weaker than Arms in PvP; this takes sustain and mobility: Improved Berserker Rage to break roots and slows, Improved Intercept for a shorter cooldown.

paladin/holy@healer#0.desc: Goes deep into Holy for every healing increase, plus Divine Intellect (Protection) and Conviction (Retribution). Last points: Pursuit of Justice and Sacred Duty.

paladin/holy@healer#1.desc: Dungeon version: adds Consecration talents for more area damage.

paladin/protection@tank#0.desc: The go-to tank build with all the strong defensive talents, keeping some offense. Anticipation gives the smoothest damage intake.

paladin/protection@tank#1.desc: Offense-leaning single-target threat: Holy Shock in the rotation, more holy damage and near-certain spell hits. Gives up a fair amount of defense.

paladin/protection@tank#2.desc: Slightly more defensive than Shockprot (5 points in Deflection, Vindication) and close to Standard in throughput; strongest against groups (cleave and area damage).

paladin/protection@tank#3.desc: Hardly a Protection build: no Protection talents, only Deflection for defense. Leans on Vengeance and Champion of the Light.

paladin/protection@tank#4.desc: Like Standard, but goes down Retribution for Pursuit of Justice, key for dungeon speed; skips Anticipation for Vindication and Guardian's Favor.

paladin/protection@tank#5.desc: Shockadin burst while off-healing, in the open world or battlegrounds. Wants some spell power on your gear.

paladin/retribution@dps#0.desc: The standard Retribution build, deep in Retribution; uses Seal of Command and Seal of Righteousness through Unsealed Wrath. Spell power and Intellect scale well (Champion of the Light).

paladin/retribution@dps#1.desc: Holy-based Shockadin: specializes in Holy and uses Seal of Righteousness. Spell power and Intellect scale well.

paladin/retribution@dps#2.desc: Almost the same as the PvE build: Deflection instead of Benediction, and Eye for an Eye instead of Holy Conduit.

paladin/retribution@dps#3.desc: Niche Shockadin with some off-healing while still dealing damage. Mana is the limit: few mana-saving talents.

hunter/beast-mastery@dps#0.desc: Pet damage and mana management. Lethal Attacks, Careful Aim and Trueshot Aura in Marksmanship also boost your pet.

hunter/beast-mastery@dps#1.desc: Keeps the big damage talents and adds Improved Concussive Shot and Improved Aspect of the Monkey; Summon Hawk is the highlight (no minimum range).

hunter/marksmanship@dps#0.desc: Pure ranged damage and mana management; with Lone Wolf no pet is needed.

hunter/marksmanship@dps#1.desc: Aimed Shot and Sniper Shot are hard to land in PvP but hit very hard; Improved Concussive Shot, Improved Stings and Scatter Shot disrupt, Survivalist and Deterrence keep you alive.

hunter/survival@dps#0.desc: Melee Survival: melee damage and mana management; Summon Hawk adds an extra button.

hunter/survival@dps#1.desc: Weaving: mixes ranged and melee damage. Survival talents raise melee damage, Marksmanship talents ranged damage.

hunter/survival@dps#2.desc: Strong in PvP at range and in melee: Summon Hawk, many defensive talents (Deterrence, Surefooted, Improved Aspect of the Monkey) and ways to stick to targets (Counterattack, traps).

priest/discipline@healer#0.desc: Healing build: deep Discipline for Power Infusion plus the essential Holy talents.

priest/discipline@healer#1.desc: Dungeon version: drops utility like Spirit Tap and Improved Inner Fire for stronger defensive picks such as Inspiration.

priest/discipline@healer#2.desc: PvP: mostly survival (Silent Resolve, Martyrdom, Blessed Recovery). Blackout is optional.

priest/holy@healer#0.desc: Discipline/Holy hybrid: Inner Focus and Penance, then Holy healing talents and Holy Nova; Wand Specialization to help kill mobs.

priest/holy@healer#1.desc: PvP: Inner Focus, Penance and Power Infusion, then Holy healing talents; favors survival and control.

priest/shadow@dps#0.desc: Raid build for damage, mana sustain and raid utility. The guide calls it still speculative.

priest/shadow@dps#1.desc: Dungeon version: adds Spirit Tap for mana when putting damage over time on many targets.

priest/shadow@dps#2.desc: A starting point for PvP: Blackout and Improved Psychic Scream for control.

shaman/elemental@dps#0.desc: Raid build with Restoration as the second tree for Mana Tide Totem, a strong cooldown for caster groups.

shaman/elemental@dps#1.desc: The second raid option, with Enhancement as the second tree.

shaman/elemental@dps#2.desc: The Shamanistic Focus raid build is likely also the best for dungeons; Mana Tide Totem is less worth it there.

shaman/elemental@dps#3.desc: PvP: Earthbound and Earth's Grasp for kiting and control, only 4 points in Tidal Focus, Lightning Mastery as the main cooldown.

shaman/elemental@dps#4.desc: PvP Elemental/Restoration hybrid with Nature's Swiftness as the main cooldown.

shaman/enhancement@dps#0.desc: Takes every relevant Enhancement talent and goes far into Elemental for spell damage.

shaman/enhancement@dps#1.desc: Dungeon version: no Rage of the Farseer and one rank of Maelstrom Weapon; finishes the hit talent in Restoration and adds Mindfulness for less drinking.

shaman/enhancement@dps#2.desc: PvP, deeper in Elemental: more spell damage and control.

shaman/enhancement@dps#3.desc: PvP, deep in Restoration: outlasts opponents and supports the team, giving up some damage and control.

shaman/restoration@healer#0.desc: All core talents: Riptide, Nature's Swiftness and Mana Tide Totem; good synergy with critical strike.

shaman/restoration@healer#1.desc: The second raid option, deeper in Restoration.

shaman/restoration@healer#2.desc: Same as the raid build: the guide finds no strong dungeon-only picks.

shaman/restoration@healer#3.desc: Like the raid build, but takes Earth's Grasp, Tidal Focus, Shamanistic Focus, Guardian Totems and Improved Ghost Wolf instead of Restorative Totems.

mage/arcane@dps#0.desc: Arcane with a Fire second tree, the guide's best option: Improved Fire Blast and Pyroblast with Heating Up, plus Missile Barrage, Arcane Wrath and Arcane Meditation.

mage/arcane@dps#1.desc: More damage in long fights by saving mana, but without Arcane Power and weaker in short fights. The guide calls it a concept until gear is tested.

mage/arcane@dps#3.desc: "Pyro PoM Pyro" PvP: very high burst every 3 minutes with Presence of Mind and Pyroblast.

mage/fire@dps#0.desc: Fire built around Fireball, with Arcane for mana and spell piercing, plus Missile Barrage.

mage/fire@dps#1.desc: The guide's second Fire option, with Frost as the second tree.

mage/fire@dps#2.desc: Classic Presence of Mind + Pyroblast PvP, with long-range Improved Fire Blast and Improved Scorch for steady damage.

mage/frost@dps#0.desc: The best deep Frost build without Frostfire Bolt; the point in Improved Blizzard enables area damage and is flexible.

mage/frost@dps#1.desc: Same as the raid build; works just as well in dungeons.

mage/frost@dps#2.desc: PvP: points move from mana saving to survival and control (Ice Block, Permafrost, Frostbite, Improved Frost Nova).

druid/feral@dps#0.desc: Lots of mana regeneration for open-world play: less drinking.

druid/feral@dps#1.desc: Pure cat damage, while also taking most talents needed to tank.

druid/feral@dps#2.desc: Hybrid: every survival talent for tanking plus the must-have cat talents.

druid/feral@dps#3.desc: Standard PvP: deep Feral for burst and deep Restoration for Swiftmend and mana regeneration.

druid/feral@tank#0.desc: All-purpose build from level 1 to 60: standard Feral talents, fully into Restoration for low mana use and little downtime.

druid/feral@tank#1.desc: The second open-world and leveling option, with Balance instead of deep Restoration.

druid/feral@tank#2.desc: Plays like a pure bear; in cat form it skips Shredding Attacks. The guide expects these builds to change.

druid/balance@dps#0.desc: Multi-DoT early, hard-cast Eclipse later for raids; move points from Reflection to Genesis if mana allows.

druid/balance@dps#1.desc: PvP: multi-DoT, keeps distance and control, survival and utility instead of mana; stays in Moonkin form.
